docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 500 g lamb (ground)
  • 10 g salt
  • 2 tsp cumin (ground)
  • 2 tbsp sumac (ground)
  • 2 tbsp Urfa pepper (flakes)
  • 2 tbsp water
  • 1 red onion (thinly sliced)

docs.title: Preparation
docs.text:
1. Combine 500 g lamb with 10 g salt, 2 tsp cumin, 2 tbsp sumac, and 2 tbsp Urfa pepper — using 7.5g salt, 1 tsp cumin, 2 tsp sumac, and 1 tbsp pepper flakes.
  2. Knead until mixture turns tacky and sticks to side of bowl. Add 2 tbsp water and knead until incorporated.
  3. Chill in refrigerator.
  4. Combine the remaining 1 tsp cumin, 2 tsp sumac, 1 tbsp pepper flakes, and 2 tsp salt in a small bowl.
  5. Combine 1 red onion and 2 tsp sumac in a medium bowl, season with salt to taste.
  6. Using wet hands, divide the lamb into 12 even balls. Form each ball into a long, flat kebab around a skewer.
  7. Cook on a grill sprinkling with the spice mixture and turning occasionally, about 12 minutes total.

docs.title: Almond-flour Carrot Muffins
docs.text: Makes ~20 muffins

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 1.5 tsp baking powder
  • 0.125 tsp salt
  • 1 tsp cinnamon
  • 0.5 tsp nutmeg
  • 2 tsp lemon zest
  • 4 eggs
  • 1 tsp vanilla extract
  • 2 cup grated carrots (10 oz)
  • 0.5 cup sugar
  • 1.5 cup almond flour (8 oz)

docs.title: Preparation
docs.text:
I use (what I think is) a baby-food freezer tray. It has 1-oz "muffin" compartments and I fill them to the brim (so probably ~1.25 oz each), this makes ~20+ muffins with that.

Typically use a granular sugar substitute like those labeled as monk-fruit extract (and typically have erythritol as well).

  1. Preheat the oven to 350°F and grease a muffin tin.
  2. Combine 1.5 tsp baking powder, 0.125 tsp salt, 1 tsp cinnamon, 0.5 tsp nutmeg, 2 tsp lemon zest, 4 eggs, 1 tsp vanilla extract, 2 cup grated carrots, and 0.5 cup sugar in a blender and blend until smooth.
  3. Add 1.5 cup almond flour to a mixing bowl, then add the contents from the blender and mix well with a spatula.
  4. Place in the muffin tin and cook for 25 minutes. Remove and let cool.

docs.text: 1. Oil roast 2 tbsp chana dhal, 2 tbsp coriander seeds, 0.25 tsp fenugreek seeds, 8 red chillies, and 2 tbsp grated coconut in 1 tbsp ghee, then set aside to cool. Once cooled, grind/blend together into a paste.

docs.text:
1. Saute 0.5 tsp mustard seeds, 10 curry leaves, and 2 green chilies in 2 tbsp ghee until fragrant and the mustard sputters.
  2. Add 0.5 tsp asafoetida and fry for 10 seconds.
  3. Add 2 onions and saute until soft.
  4. Add the masala paste, 2 tomatoes, 1 lbs pumpkin, 0.5 cup toor dhal, 1 tsp turmeric powder, salt to taste, and additional water to preference (1 liter).
  5. Cook on high in a pressure cooker for 8 minutes and allow a natural (slow) release.
  6. Once cooked, add 1 tsp jaggery (if using) and mix well, then garnish with 1 bunch cilantro and serve.

docs.title: Preparation
docs.text:
1. Melt 0.25 cup ghee in a pressure cooker pot.

docs.title: Buttery Roasted Parsnips with Mole Crunch
Ingredients
docs.text:
• 0.5 cup Mole Crunch
  • 0.25 cup kosher salt
  • 2 pounds parsnips
  • 0.25 cup unsalted butter

docs.title: Preparation
docs.text:
1. Pre-heat the oven to 425°F.
  2. Fill a large pot with water and start to boil, then add 0.25 cup kosher salt.
  3. Trim 2 pounds parsnips and cut in half across their width (where they begin to taper). Cut the top halves along their length to match the width of the bottom half.
  4. Boil the parsnips for 4-6 minutes, until slightly firm but pliable.
  5. Drain the water and add 0.25 cup unsalted butter to the parsnips, tossing it so it melts.
  6. Spread the parsnips on a baking sheet.
  7. Roast on the center rack until tender and caramelized.
  8. Pile parsnips on a serving platter and sprinkle with 0.5 cup mole-crunch.

  5. Let the mixture cool a bit and pour it into your choice of container (sheet-cake pan, popsicle sticks, ice-cube trays, small cups, etc.).
  6. Place in the freezer until frozen solid and serve.

docs.text:
• 1.5 lb chicken (sliced)

  • 0.25 cup coconut cream
  • 3 tbsp red curry paste
  • 2 tbsp yellow curry paste
  • 2 tbsp palm sugar
  • 3 tbsp, 0.25 cup fish sauce
  • 1.5 cup coconut milk

  • 6 oz extra-firm tofu (sliced into 1/4" sticks)
  • 2 tsp curry powder
  • 8 oz mung bean sprouts

  • 0.25 cup preserved radish (finely chopped)
  • 0.25 cup fried shallots
  • 0.25 cup cilantro (chopped)

  • 2 medium-boiled egg (halved)
  • 3 limes (in wedges)
  • 0.25 cup granulated sugar
  • 2 tbsp red chile powder

docs.title: Preparation
docs.text:
1. Cut 1.5 lb chicken against the grain into bite-size slices, set aside.
  2. Cook 1 tbsp oil, 0.25 cup coconut cream, 3 tbsp red curry paste, and 2 tbsp yellow curry paste in a medium or large pot for 2 minutes.
  3. Add the chicken and stir to coat with paste, then cook 1 minute.
  4. Add 2 tbsp palm sugar, 3 tbsp fish sauce, 1.5 cup coconut milk, and 3 cup chicken stock; stir well and cook until the chicken is cooked.
  5. Add 6 oz extra-firm tofu and 2 tsp curry powder, mix well and set the pot to simmer.
  6. Heat water to boil, blanch 8 oz mung bean sprouts (very quickly).
  7. Cook 8 oz rice noodles in the same water.
  8. Divide noodles and sprouts into bowls.
  9. Ladle the curry over the noodles, sprinkle with 0.25 cup preserved radish, 0.25 cup fried shallots, 0.25 cup cilantro, and 0.33 cup roasted peanuts.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 500 g all-purpose flour
  • 10 g kosher salt
  • 4 g instant dry yeast
  • 400 g room temperature water
  • 67 g extra-virgin olive oil
  • coarse sea salt

docs.title: Make the Dough
docs.text:
1. Combine 500 g all-purpose flour, 10 g kosher salt, and 4 g instant dry yeast in a bowl.
  2. Mix in 400 g room temperature water and stir until no dry flour remains.
  3. Add 20 g extra-virgin olive oil, use hands to work it into the dough.
  4. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and let rest at room temperature for 1 hour.
  5. Remove the plastic wrap. Using a greased scraper, fold the dough over itself (lift and fold one edge toward the middle). Rotate 45 degrees and repeat for 6 total folds.
  6. Cover and let rest for 15 minutes, then repeat the folding sequence again.
  7. Cover the bowl tightly with plastic wrap and store in refrigerator for 18-72 hours to cold proof.

docs.title: Bake
docs.text:
1. Remove the dough from the refrigerator and let sit at room temperature for 10 minutes.
  2. Sprinkle with flour, then transfer the dough to a floured working surface. Tuck the dough underneath itself until it forms a tight ball.
  3. Pour 27 g extra-virgin olive oil into a 10 or 12 inch skillet (or other baking pan) and spread over the entire surface, including the rim.
  4. Place the dough in the pan seam-side down and coat in oil. Spread the dough out to flatten — don't worry if it doesn't reach the edges.
  5. Cover tightly and let sit for a final proof of 1.5-2 hours, until soft and puffy.
  6. One hour before baking, preheat the oven to 500°F and place a baking stone or steel on the lower-middle rack.
  7. Once the dough is puffy, use oiled fingers to press it to the edges of the pan, lifting in places to allow air bubbles to escape.
  8. Create small dimples in the dough surface with your fingers and drizzle 20 g extra-virgin olive oil over the dough.
  9. Sprinkle with coarse sea salt.
  10. Place the skillet on top of the baking stone or steel and bake for 25-30 minutes, rotating the pan 180 degrees halfway through.
  11. Let the bread rest for 5 minutes after removing from the oven, then brush with a little more oil.
  12. Let cool for 10 minutes before serving.

docs.title: Fragrant Beets and Cherries with Cashew Butter
Ingredients
docs.text:
• 1.5 pound red beets
  • 0.75 cup red wine vinegar
  • 0.333 cup olive oil
  • 2 tbsp kosher salt
  • 0.333 cup dried chamomile flowers
  • 0.333 cup dried hibiscus flowers
  • 0.5 cup cashew butter
  • 0.5 tsp salt
  • 1 tbsp lemon juice
  • 0.5 pound cherries (pitted and halved)
  • 0.5 cup roasted cashews (chopped)
  • flaky sea salt
  • black pepper (ground)
  • 0.5 cup mint leaves

docs.title: Preparation
docs.text:
The first few times I did this I used dried cherries instead of fresh and it turned out really good. If you do this, use ~half the stated mass (dried cherries are much lighter).

Substitute cashew butter and/or roasted cashews for other nut butters and/or nuts as needed. Sunflower butter and roasted pistachios is a good combination.

  1. Pre-heat the oven to 375°F.
  2. Place 1.5 pound red beets in a dish just big enough to fit them.
  3. Mix 0.75 cup red wine vinegar, 0.333 cup olive oil, 2 tbsp kosher salt, 0.333 cup dried chamomile flowers, and 0.333 cup dried hibiscus flowers.
  4. Pour the liquid mixture over the beets into their dish.
  5. Cover the beets with parchment paper and foil, sealing tightly around the lip of the dish.
  6. Place the dish in the oven. After an hour, check for doneness (it usually takes a while). If not done, add water (if needed), reseal, and place back in the oven. Check again every 20 minutes until done.
  7. When done, remove from oven and rotate the beets face down into the liquid (upside down from how they cooked) and let cool. If you're in a hurry, you can dump the beets in ice-water to cool them.
  8. Using your hands, peel the beets and rip them into bite-sized chunks, place in a bowl and set aside.
  9. Combine 0.5 cup cashew butter, 0.5 tsp salt, 1 tbsp lemon juice, and 2 tbsp water; mix thoroughly, adding water until it is easily spreadable.
  10. Spread the cashew butter on a serving platter, then top with the beets.
  11. Sprinkle with some lemon juice and olive oil.
  12. Top with 0.5 pound cherries, 0.5 cup roasted cashews, flaky sea salt, black pepper, and 0.5 cup mint leaves.

docs.title: Frijoles Charros
docs.text: Serves 10

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 1 lb pinto beans
  • 1 tbsp salt
  • 1 tbsp baking soda
  • 6 cups stock (optional)
  • 3 bay leaves (optional)
  • 3 epazote sprigs (optional)
  • 0.5 lb bacon (chopped)
  • 1 onion (chopped)
  • 1 jalapeno (chopped)
  • 3 garlic cloves (minced)
  • 28 oz fire roasted tomatoes (canned)

docs.title: Beans
docs.text:
1. Rinse and soak 1 lb pinto beans with 1 tbsp salt and 1 tbsp baking soda for 12 hours, thoroughly rinse beans once done soaking.
  2. Bring pinto beans to boil in 6 cups stock with 3 bay leaves and 3 epazote sprigs, then let simmer for 45 min.

    You can omit the stock and herbs here if you don't have them, still comes out pretty good.

docs.title: Gravy
docs.text:
1. Fry 0.5 lb bacon in a large skillet or pot.

    I use scissors to cut them into little pieces.

  2. Add 1 onion and 1 jalapeno and continue frying until they are soft and fragrant.

    Can substitute serrano or other chili as well, if you want it less spice, be sure to remove all the seeds and pith before chopping.

  3. Add 3 garlic cloves and fry for 30 sec (make sure it does not overcook and become bitter).
  4. Add 28 oz fire roasted tomatoes and let simmer until the gravy thickens. > for a smoother texture, consider running an ?immersion blender in the gravy until you get your desired consistency.

docs.title: Combine
docs.text:
1. Add gravy to the cooked beans and let simmer all together for 20 min.
  2. Optionally, use an immersion blender to blender some of the beans so the whole dish is creamier.

docs.title: For big batches
docs.text: 1. Alternatively, you can make a big batch of gravy and freeze it to add to cooked beans later. If doing so, add the epazote and bay leaves to the gravy. Fry the bacon, then combine all other ingredients and cook on high for 45 minutes and let it naturally release. Blend gravy then portion out to freeze. You can use as little as 1/2 of this gravy recipe for a lb of beans and still have decent results.

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 1 portion Sweet Sticky Rice
  • 5 bananas (small)
  • 2 tbsp lime juice
  • 2 cup coconut cream
  • 1 pinch salt
  • 0.25 cup palm sugar
  • 2 tbsp black coconut sugar
  • 2 pandanus leaves (knotted)
  • 2 tbsp turmeric (finely chopped)
  • 0.25 cup coconut cream for serving

docs.title: Preparation
docs.text:
This is a much less sweet version of the original. It uses 1/8th the sugar of the original, but I think it is still sufficiently sweet.

  1. Make 1 portion sweet-sticky-rice.
  2. Peel 5 bananas and steep in water mixed with 2 tbsp lime juice while working on other items.

docs.title: Sauce
docs.text: 1. Combine 2 cup coconut cream, 1 pinch salt, 0.25 cup palm sugar, 2 tbsp black coconut sugar, 2 pandanus leaves, and 2 tbsp turmeric in a pot and simmer until thickened (7-10 minutes).

This is a much less sweet version of the original. It uses 1/6th the sugar of the original, but I think it is still sufficiently sweet.

  1. Soak 2 cup dry sticky rice (sometimes called sweet or glutinous rice) overnight (can do quicker, but at least 2 hours).
  2. Steam in a cheesecloth (can be with a traditional sticky rice steamer, but I've had plenty of success with the stainless-steel western steamers).
  3. While the rice is cooking, mix 2 cup coconut milk, 0.25 cup sugar, 2 tbsp palm sugar, and 1 tsp salt and simmer until the sugar is dissolved.
  4. When the rice is complete, put in a dish just big enough to hold it and pour the warm sauce over it. Allow to soak for a bit before serving.

  • 2 black cardamom (optional)
  • 1 tsp turmeric powder
  • 3 fresh chilies (split)

docs.title: Preparation
docs.text: We found this while looking for a replication of Zyka's chicken kalimirch (https://zyka.com/menu). It's not a perfect substitute, but still very good.

docs.title: Marinate
docs.text:
1. Cut 800 gram chicken into bite-sized pieces.
  2. Mix 0.5 tsp black peppercorns, 2 tbsp lemon juice, 0.5 tsp salt, 2 tsp ginger, and 4 cloves garlic in a bowl, then mix the chicken into that. Let marinate for 30 minutes.

docs.title: Spice Mix
docs.text:
1. Toast 2 tsp black peppercorns, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp fennel seeds, 3 cloves, 1 tbsp coriander seeds, and 1 dried chili in a skillet on the stove (if any of the spices are not whole, put them in at the end so they do not burn).
  2. Let the toasted spices cool, then grind in a spice grinder or mortar and pestle.

docs.title: Masala
docs.text:
1. Heat 1 tbsp coconut oil in a pan, add 15 curry leaves, 7 cm cinnamon, 2 onion, and some salt. Saute until the onions start to brown.
  2. Add 2 tomatoes and 2 black cardamom and cook until the tomatoes become mushy.
  3. Add the spice mix and 1 tsp turmeric powder and saute for a minute.
  4. Increase to high heat, add the chicken and 3 fresh chilies and mix well, add water if needed (to prevent burning), then turn the heat down to simmer and cover. Cook for 30 minutes, check/stir periodically to prevent sticking. You may need to add some water.
  5. Once the chicken is soft, remove the top and turn the heat up to cook off liquid (to your liking, usually the curry is eaten dry).
  6. Let rest for a few minutes before serving.

docs.title: Preparation
docs.text:
1. Put 2 pounds roma tomatoes, 1 onion, 1 cup carrots, 2 cup zucchini, 2 cloves garlic, 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp dried oregano, 400 ml coconut milk, 1 tsp salt, and 0.5 tsp black pepper in the pressure cooker and mix (mostly so the liquid is well distributed and things don't burn).

  4. Add 10 leaves fresh basil.

docs.title: Preparation
docs.text:
For the liquid sweetener, the original recipe calls for light corn syrup; we usually use either honey or maple syrup.

  1. Combine 1.75 cup coconut milk, 1.75 cup coconut cream, 0.25 cup liquid sweetener, 0.75 cup sugar, and 0.5 tsp salt in a sauce pan on medium heat and bring to a simmer (be sure to stir so nothing burns).
  2. Blend the mixture (either traditional or immersion blender is fine).
  3. Mix in 2 tsp vanilla extract and pour into an airtight container, put in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours.
  4. Once chilled, churn in an ice cream maker.
  5. Once the ice cream is done, you can eat immediately (for a much softer ice cream) or put in an air tight container in the freezer for at least 5 hours to stiffen.

Serves 4

docs.title: Ingredients
docs.text:
• 1 cup flour
  • 0.5 tbsp baking powder
  • 0.125 tsp baking soda
  • 0.5 tsp salt
  • 4 tbsp unsalted butter
  • 0.5 cup yogurt

docs.title: Preparation
docs.text:
1. Combine 1 cup flour, 0.5 tbsp baking powder, 0.125 tsp baking soda, and 0.5 tsp salt.
  2. Pre-heat the oven to 425°F.
  3. Cut 4 tbsp unsalted butter into roughly 0.25-in x 0.25-in cubes and cut into the dry ingredients.
  4. Add 0.5 cup yogurt, fold into the mixture with a spatula.
  5. Flatten and fold onto itself several times (to make the flakes).
  6. Flatten one last time to roughly 0.5–0.75 inches thick, cut biscuits to desired size.
  7. Place biscuits on a greased cooking pan and cook for 15 minutes (until golden brown on top).
